risks.title: Dependence on a single manufacturing site
risks.summary: CytoMed Therapeutics relies entirely on its manufacturing facility in Johor, Malaysia, to produce its cell therapies. Any disruption (fire, pandemic, regulatory failure) could halt production and delay clinical trials.
risks.score_rationale: Risk is mentioned in the RISK FACTORS section, with strong language on potential operational impact. It is stable compared to the previous year. The Industrial category is critical for a live therapy player. Central position in the document.

risks.title: Intense competition in cell therapies
risks.summary: The cell and gene therapy market is highly competitive, with companies such as Novartis, Gilead, and BMS. As a small company, CytoMed risks losing market share or failing to secure partnerships.
risks.score_rationale: Strong language on competitive pressure, with references to major global players. Risk is increasing due to sector expansion. Positioned early in risk factors. Major strategic category.

risks.title: Strict regulation of CTGTP in Singapore
risks.summary: CytoMed is subject to Singapore's strict regulations on cell and gene therapy products (CTGTP). Any delay or denial of approval by the HSA could block the development or commercialization of its drug candidates.
risks.score_rationale: Text explicitly cites HPA, CTGTP Regulations, and HSA. Demanding and detailed language. Risk is stable but fundamental. High position in the document. Key category for the biotech sector.

risks.title: Dependence on key technology partnerships
risks.summary: CytoMed relies on exclusive licenses with ATPL for critical technologies such as NK cell expansion and know-how (Know-How License). Loss of these agreements would severely impact its R&D pipeline.
risks.score_rationale: Specific references to licenses with ATPL and Puricell. Language indicating operational dependency. Risk is stable. Core Technology category for innovation. Notable position in definitions.

risks.title: Insufficient intellectual property protection
risks.summary: CytoMed may not effectively protect its inventions, particularly in gamma delta T cells and iPSC. Third parties could challenge its patents or develop similar technologies, weakening its competitive position.
risks.score_rationale: Explicit mention of risk regarding IP position and litigation. Concerned language. Risk is increasing with portfolio expansion. Strategic category. Positioned in key factors.

risks.title: Cybersecurity of sensitive clinical data
risks.summary: As a developer of advanced therapies, CytoMed handles sensitive clinical and genomic data. A cybersecurity breach could compromise trials, damage reputation, and lead to regulatory penalties.
risks.score_rationale: Dedicated section ITEM 16K on cybersecurity. Cautious but concerned language. Risk is new or reinforced. Category growing in importance. Late but specific position.

risks.title: Dependence on sole specialized suppliers
risks.summary: CytoMed depends on specialized suppliers for rare reagents, equipment, or raw materials (e.g., stem cells, viral vectors). A supply disruption could delay production or clinical trials.
risks.score_rationale: Implied mention through critical supply chain for live therapies. Cautious language. Risk is stable. Key operational category. Positioned in logistical risks.

risks.title: Dependence on key researchers and clinicians
risks.summary: CytoMed's success relies on close collaborations with leading researchers and clinicians (e.g., ANGELICA trial with NUH). Loss of these relationships or key talent could slow clinical development.
risks.score_rationale: Reference to collaborations with institutes such as CRIS, IMCB, and NUH. Language emphasizing value of academic partnerships. Risk is stable. Critical human category. Positioned in strategic agreements.
